newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- price gains seen uneven.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- price gains seen uneven.

text.p: Lesser-quality, high grade U.S. municipal bonds outperformed issues with better ratings at the intermediate part of the yield curve, rising as much as one-quarter of a point.

But at the long-end, prices were mainly seen from flat to up around one-eighth of a point. The slightly jagged performance turned in by various sectors led at least one municipal analyst to fret that the market might not be able to continue to outpace the Treasury market.

"When other bonds start not to move, and you've got your (Treasury) ratios down below 82 percent, which we are tonight, and are up in the long-end near a 52-week high, the Treasury market has got to do something fairly strong and firm, or we may get ourselves into trouble," said a municipal analyst.

Though supplies of new issues are forecast to fatten this week to around $3.4 billion, the recent sales drought has helped the municipal market remain fairly strong when compared to the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond.
And traders said that several new offerings sold on Tuesday appeared to command attractive prices.
"I thought they were nice, firm deals," the municipal analyst said.
For example, Smith Barney cut the top yield in 2017 by five basis points to 5.475 percent in a $155 million sale by Platte River Power of Colorado.
But the Auburn School District in Washington, which sold $38 million of debt, was forced to raise yields in the 2012 to 2014 maturities by as much as five basis points.

One of the deals slated for Wednesday, a nearly $490 million offering by the Municipal Assistance Corporation for New York City, only got about $58.7 million of orders during the second and last day of the retail pre-sale period, said a source familiar with the transaction.
This was less than the approximately $80 million of retail orders that the MAC got for a roughly $677 million refunding in December.

In the Chicago futures markets, the March U.S. municipal bond ended five ticks higher at 117-3/32, while the March U.S. Treasury bonds edged down one tick to 112-19/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 144 ticks.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of January 2023, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.58 percent NET, down one basis point.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey, which mature on January 2026 and pay 1 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.61 percent, also down one basis point.
